newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end up despite lack of news.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end up despite lack of news.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Tuesday's Tokyo session higher.
There was no particular news that encouraged buying, but the March contract closed up 0.32 at 125.62 amid an absence of sellers.
"Large-lot bids had pushed the March to an intraday high of 125.72 early in the afternoon," a brokerage house trader said.
Some dealers who had earlier created short positions for hedging purposes covered their shorts after seeing investors' demand for cash JGBs, a Japanese bank trader said.
Investors, however, were reluctant to chase the yield below 2.40 percent, traders said.
"Investors remained keen to buy on dips, but were not very eager to buy below 2.40 percent," said another brokerage house trader.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.400 percent as of 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), after falling as low as 2.390 percent.
"Investors have very few alternatives to invest in. Hence, they should continue to look for opportunities to buy JGBs," a trader at a city bank's securities unit said.
"Unless this favourable demand-supply condition changes, the downside is likely to be limited," he added.
The absence of major domestic economic data releases this week is diverting market participants' attention to external factors.
However, today's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting is unlikely to have any impact as the Fed is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, traders said.
On Wednesday, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita is scheduled to give a news conference at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT).
If Matsushita simply repeats his recent remarks that Japan's economy was recovering gradually, the JGB market is unlikely to react, traders said.

On Wednesday, Japan's money supply data and customs-cleared trade figures for November will be released at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT Tuesday), but they are not expected to have any major impact on the JGB market, traders said. -- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
